why: The row's numbers are on the page, but the generalisation is contradicted by the very table quoted. GenEval columns are Overall / Single Obj. / Two Obj. / Counting / Colors / Position / Color attribution. PixArt-alpha reads '0.48 0.98 0.50 0.44 0.80 0.08 0.07' — Color attribution 0.07 is BELOW Position 0.08. Janus-Pro-7B reads '0.80 0.99 0.89 0.59 0.90 0.79 0.66' — Position 0.79 is its second-best axis; Counting 0.59 is its worst. Both are open-weight and both are in the table, and Janus-Pro-7B is silently omitted from the harvester's enumeration. 'Position remains the worst GenEval axis for every open-weight model in the table' is false as written.
value: Position remains the worst GenEval axis for every open-weight model in the table — SDXL 0.15, PixArt-alpha 0.08, FLUX.1-dev 0.22, SD3-Medium 0.33, CogView4-6B 0.48, and even the table's winner HiDream-I1 only 0.60 against 1.00 on Single Object. Compositional/spatial prompts are the class-wide failure, and headline 'overall' scores of 0.66-0.83 conceal it.

why: github.com and api.github.com both answered 403 for this unattached repo, so I read data/leaderboards.json from a clone of SWE-bench/swe-bench.github.io at f42505b. Both rows exist on the Verified leaderboard with exactly the stated numbers (74.2 / 40.326 calls / $0.45996 and 69.6 / 51.282 calls / $0.96002). But the row's load-bearing premise is contradicted by the data: these are NOT the same model id. One is gemini-3-pro-preview-20251118 (a preview snapshot, no reasoning_effort field); the other is gemini-3-pro at reasoning_effort 'high'. Model version and reasoning effort both change alongside the harness version, so the source does not support attributing the 4.6-point drop to mini-SWE-agent 1.15.0 vs 2.0.0. The general lesson ('a leaderboard number is a harness+model measurement') may well be true, but this page does not measure it.
value: The same model id under two versions of the SAME minimal agent harness differs by 4.6 points on SWE-bench Verified: gemini-3-pro-preview scored 74.2% on 2025-11-18 under mini-SWE-agent 1.15.0 (40.3 API calls, $0.46/instance) and 69.6% on 2026-02-26 under mini-SWE-agent 2.0.0 at high reasoning effort (51.3 calls, $0.96/instance). A leaderboard number is a harness+model measurement, not a model measurement.

why: arxiv.org answered 200 but the fetch is capped at 400000 bytes; the HTML stops inside section 5.3.2 (Figure 18, long English text rendering), before section 5.3.3 on image editing where the quoted sentence would sit. Grep for 'zoom-in and zoom-out' over the retrieved text returns nothing. The PDF at arxiv.org/pdf/2508.02324v1 comes back as truncated binary, and huggingface.co/papers/2508.02324 carries only the abstract. No mirror or cache attempted per policy. Note also the source is the Qwen-Image Technical Report (a vendor paper), not a neutral benchmark, so the class-wide scope would need the actual sentence read to stand.
value: Class-wide editing artifact: instruction-edit models silently rescale the frame, so a nominally local edit returns a differently-cropped image. Fatal for any pipeline that composites edited frames back into a fixed layout.

why: The quotation IS on the page (arXiv:2509.16941v2, Table 4 caption), but the value the harvester attached to it is not what the page says: it misreads the table's columns. In Table 4, 72.8% / 27.9% / 52.7% are the Not-Submitted column, not wrong-solution. Read from the page: 'GPT-5 (high) 27.2% 72.8% 39.5% ...' (Submitted 27.2%, Not-Submitted 72.8%, Wrong Solution 39.5%); 'GPT-4o 72.1% 27.9% 45.2%' (Wrong Solution 45.2%); 'Qwen3 32B 47.3% 52.7% 25.0%' (Wrong Solution 25.0%). The stated conclusion 'weaker models fail earlier in the pipeline, not later' is also contradicted — GPT-5 (high) has the HIGHEST not-submitted rate of the six. The bucket list is likewise off: the table's buckets are Wrong Solution, Syntax Error, Incorrect File, Instruction Following, Edge Case, Other, Tool-Use, Long-Context, Stuck in Loop — 'Endless File Reading' and 'Misunderstood Problem Statement' are not column headers. Reject on the numbers, not on reachability.
value: SWE-Bench Pro failure buckets for agent trajectories, LLM-as-a-judge classified: Wrong solution, Tool-Use, Syntax error, Incorrect file, Endless File Reading, Misunderstood Problem Statement, Other. GPT-5 (high) failures are 72.8% wrong-solution; GPT-4o 27.9%, Qwen3 32B 52.7% — weaker models fail earlier in the pipeline, not later.
